text.p: Italian debt markets shadowed other bond markets to end a choppy day's trade between 10 and 20 basis points higher.
The February 2006 Btp was 10 basis points up at 103.35 while the December future on LIFFE strained up to 118.33 and then crept back to stand 22 basis points up at 117.96 in late trade.

Comments from a Federal Reserve official that the Fed consensus was for a 25 basis point fed funds target rate hike and a 50 basis point increase in the discount rate at the next FOMC meeting on September 24 took their toll on bond markets.

A raft of European monetary union comments from Bundesbank officials and German and French Ministers caused ripples through the market. However BTps retained their grip on a spread of just under 300 basis points against Germany, unchanged from Monday.

But some traders were sceptical of the Italian bonds' recent gains, saying BTps were piggybacking on a more positive international situation. They sounded a warning note for possible problems in parliament over the government's 1997 budget package, currently being prepared for presentation by the end of the month.
